This was then compared with the time at which certain brain events, measured by EEG, occurred in the subject. These were brain events which other experiments had shown to precede certain intentional actions. The increased brain activity which occurs prior to a certain sort of intentional action is called that action’s readiness potential. Libet called the times at which subjects showed a readiness potential for flexing their hands “RP-onset times.”
The W time and the RP-onset time were then compared with the “zero time” — the time at which the subject’s hand actually flexed.
